Mental Health Care Plan

Patient & GP Details

- Patient: Valerie Cole, DOB: 19/09/1993, Gender: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded, Address: 64 Cliveden Place, South Wimbledon
- Referring GP: Doctor Smith, Practice: Babylon, Practice Address: Not recorded. Provider No.: Not recorded, Contact: Not recorded

Clinical Assessment

Identified Problems/Provisional Diagnoses:
- Principal: Anxiety symptoms — marked morning/anticipatory anxiety about leaving house and attending work, palpitations, sleep disturbance (insomnia) — temporally related to starting a new job ~2 months ago (provisional)
- Secondary: Low mood / anhedonia related to ongoing anxiety
- Tertiary: Avoidance of social activities and reduced engagement in hobbies; increased alcohol intake at weekends (patient-reported)

Clinical Details & History:
- Medications: Not recorded
- Allergies/ADRs: Not recorded
- Past Medical History: Not recorded

Mental Health History:
- Previous Diagnoses: Not recorded (patient reports no previous similar episodes)
- Past Treatments (Therapy, Medications, Hospitalizations): No prior therapy or psychiatric medication reported; has not sought previous professional treatment for current symptoms
- Family History: Mother has a history of depression (patient reports)

Social & Lifestyle Factors:
- Living Situation: Lives with parents
- Social Support: Good family support (mother/family supportive)
- Occupation/Education: Employed at a fashion retailer head office team; new role started ~2 months ago; describes boss as "not very nice"; job-related stress prominent
- Alcohol Use: Patient reports drinking "quite a lot" on Friday/Saturday and a glass occasionally during the week; exact quantity not recorded
- Smoking/Substance Use: Occasionally smokes; denies recreational drug use
- Key Stressors: Recent new and stressful job, difficult manager, anticipatory work-related anxiety, public transport anxiety

Mental Status Examination (MSE):
- Appearance & General Behaviour: Cooperative, communicative; appeared distressed by symptoms (patient reported distress)
- Mood & Affect: Anxious and low mood; reports feeling "down" and reduced enjoyment
- Speech & Thought: Speech coherent and goal-directed; no evidence of formal thought disorder recorded
- Perception: No hallucinations or perceptual disturbances reported

Cognition:
- Orientation: Not recorded
- Attention/Concentration: Not recorded
- Memory: Not recorded
- Insight & Judgement: Good insight into symptoms; engaged in seeking help and receptive to therapy/referrals

Physical Symptoms:
- Sleep: Difficulty falling asleep, shallow sleep, estimates ~3–4 hours per night, frequently awake with racing heart/panic in mornings
- Appetite: No significant change reported; increased consumption of chocolate
- Motivation/Energy: Markedly reduced energy and motivation; anhedonia (loss of enjoyment in previously pleasurable activities)
- Anxiety Symptoms: Morning anticipatory anxiety, palpitations (patient describes irregular rapid heartbeats lasting minutes up to ~10 minutes), panic-like symptoms on waking, avoidance of social activities and public transport

Risk Assessment
- Suicidal/Self-Harm/Risk to Others: Patient explicitly denies suicidal thoughts; no self-harm or risk to others reported
- Protective Factors: Good family support; insight into problem; stable engagement with work (has continued to attend)
- Overall Current Risk Level (Self): Low (no suicidal ideation reported; protective factors present)
- Emergency Contact: Not recorded

Formulation
- Predisposing factors: No prior similar severe episodes reported; family history of depression (mother)
- Precipitating factors: Recent new job (~2 months), difficult manager, increased job-related stress and long working hours
- Perpetuating factors: Insomnia and anticipatory morning panic, avoidance of social/leisure activities, increased alcohol on weekends, ongoing exposure to stressful workplace
- Protective factors: Good family support, insight, willingness to engage with talking therapy and online resources, continued attendance at work

Mental Health Care Plan Details

Principal Problem: Anxiety (work-related) with morning panic/palpitations and insomnia
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Reduce morning anxiety and panic symptoms
  - Improve sleep quantity and quality
  - Return to enjoying previously valued activities
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Provide timely access to evidence-based psychological therapy (NHS talking therapies/IAPT)
  - Exclude reversible medical causes for palpitations (basic blood tests)
  - Provide brief self-help resources and sleep hygiene advice; monitor response and need for medication if persistent/severe
- Actions (Patient):
  - Self-refer to NHS talking therapy (patient agreed to self-refer)
  - Contact support line to arrange blood tests as advised
  - Use recommended online resources/supportive self-help while awaiting therapy
  - Monitor symptoms and re-contact GP/clinician if anxiety worsens or becomes unmanageable
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Provide link/information for NHS talking therapy/self-help resources and add sleep hygiene information to notes (clinician indicated will do so)
  - Recommend and arrange basic blood tests to investigate palpitations and potential contributors; arrange GP follow-up ~1 week after tests to review results
  - Advise patient to re-contact service if symptoms escalate or impair ability to function
  - Consider pharmacological treatment for anxiety in future if therapy and self-help are insufficient (not first-line at present)

Secondary Problem: Low mood / anhedonia
- Patient Goal(s):
  - Improve mood and re-engage with social and leisure activities
- Clinical Goal(s):
  - Assess and treat underlying anxiety contributing to low mood; prevent development of major depressive disorder
- Actions (Patient):
  - Engage with talking therapy and recommended self-help resources
  - Attempt gradual re-engagement with social/leisure activities as tolerable
  - Limit alcohol intake where possible (patient-reported increased drinking at weekends)
- Actions (Clinician/GP):
  - Monitor mood and suicidal ideation at follow-up contacts
  - Offer referral to psychological therapies (IAPT) and consider primary care interventions (including review for antidepressant if deterioration or insufficient response to therapy)

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention
- Education Given: Yes. Topics Covered: nature of anxiety; recommendation for NHS talking therapy/self-referral; online self-help resources; sleep hygiene information to be provided; palpitations likely anxiety-related but basic blood tests recommended; instruction to contact service if unable to cope.
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening:
  - Increasing frequency or severity of panic or anticipatory anxiety preventing attendance at work
  - Development of suicidal thoughts or intent
  - Marked functional decline or inability to perform day-to-day activities
- Coping Strategies:
  - Use of recommended online CBT/self-help resources (clinician recommended)
  - Sleep hygiene strategies (information to be provided)
  - Contact clinician/GP if symptoms worsen or become unmanageable

Consent, Coordination & Review
- Patient Consent to Plan: Yes — patient agreed to self-refer to talking therapy and to arrange blood tests
- Copy of Mental Health Care Plan Given to Patient: Not recorded
- Other Mental Health Professionals Involved in Patient Care: Not recorded
- GP Acknowledgment (if completed by other MH Professional): Not recorded
- Review Date: GP follow-up arranged approximately 1 week after blood tests (patient instructed to call support line to arrange tests)

Quality checks
● Missing but clinically expected elements: exact diagnosis (formal diagnostic code), medication list, allergies, past medical history, detailed suicide risk assessment documentation, emergency contact details, quantification of alcohol intake, objective vital signs or ECG (not recorded).  
● Internal conflicts from the transcript: None noted. (Patient reports no suicidal ideation but reports increased alcohol use and significant functional impact; conflict not identified.)  
● Transcript quality notes: Audio/dialogue clear; some numeric details not provided (contact numbers, exact alcohol quantity, smoking frequency, no explicit orientation/cognitive testing).
